capabilities: hide most Obsidian UI elements while a note or document stays visible
toggle Zen mode and restore the UI with a single button
collapse and restore the side bars when toggling
configure padding, full screen, hidden properties and inline title options
temporarily reveal the note header when title focus is requested
extras: Theme developers are told that ZenMode injects a zenmode-active class on the body element when active; the README also lists a TODO to refactor duplicated CSS.
intentEvidence: An Obsidian Zen-Mode pluigin based on the Hider plugin.
motivation: Obsidian is by default unfit for content consumption or presentations.
problem: Obsidian's default UI takes up much of the screen, especially on mobile where viewing a PDF can leave under 40% of the screen for content, and there is no quick switch between an editing layout and a viewing layout.

relations.evidence: An Obsidian Zen-Mode pluigin based on the Hider plugin.

summary: UI-hiding plugin that strips away most of Obsidian's interface so only the current file remains, with one button to restore it.
